output.brief: The rise is probably not caused by the self-checkout lanes. They were offline from 2 April to 26 June, yet shrink rose through Q2, and Q3 self-checkout loss rates were normal. The mix of departments also barely changed. The stocker tip was checked on CCTV and closed as unsubstantiated, and the evidence does not point at staff theft. Incident counts jumped when the chain-wide incident app launched on 1 April, so the logging change may account for some of the rise. Interim figures carry about ±0.6 points of error per quarter. The store's full-count history was flat (1.6, 1.8, 1.5). My confidence is moderate: the December full count is the real test. Next steps: keep store 14 in the 7 December count and decline the proposal to drop it. Hold off on a door guard or any personnel action. Compare the full count with the interim figures, and check whether incident rises are real or come from the new app.
